checklist.label: Numbering and traumatic alignment
checklist.detail: Name the vertebra or motion segment and assess translation, rotation, distraction and focal angulation; document numbering and coverage limits.

checklist.label: Vertebral fracture morphology
checklist.detail: Map vertebral-body walls, one or both endplates and each posterior element. Distinguish compression/burst morphology, posterior-wall retropulsion and a transosseous distraction pattern. Note relevant bone or marrow abnormality and fracture-age evidence using the acquired modality and comparison.

checklist.label: Posterior tension band
checklist.detail: Assess spinous/interspinous and facet relationships on CT. On acquired MRI, assess supraspinous and interspinous ligaments, ligamenta flava and facet capsules separately; distinguish definite disruption from indeterminate oedema.

checklist.label: Discs and longitudinal ligaments
checklist.detail: Assess traumatic disc-space widening or disruption, endplate interfaces and anterior/posterior longitudinal ligaments with the available modality, including anterior distraction in a rigid spine.

checklist.label: Canal, epidural and neural structures
checklist.detail: Localise canal, lateral-recess or foraminal encroachment and epidural abnormality. On acquired MRI, describe cord, conus, cauda equina and named root compression or signal abnormality within coverage.

checklist.label: Paraspinal and associated injury
checklist.detail: Describe paraspinal or prevertebral soft-tissue injury, additional included fractures, postoperative limitations and other relevant visible abnormalities.

checklist.label: Classification inputs and clinical neurology
checklist.detail: Keep imaging morphology and posterior ligamentous complex assessment separate from supplied clinical neurological status. Name the applicable AO/TLICS assessment and document missing clinical information.

measurements.name: Vertebral deformity
measurements.method: At each injured level, describe vertebral height loss and local angulation with the measured surfaces, plane and comparison reference.
measurements.pitfall: Height loss or angulation alone does not determine ligament integrity, neurological status or treatment.

measurements.name: Retropulsion and canal encroachment
measurements.method: Measure posterior-wall retropulsion in mm on a stated plane/reference. If canal narrowing is quantified, identify the diameter or area method and reference level; describe the actual compartment affected.
measurements.pitfall: Do not interchange diameter and area percentages or infer clinical cord injury from osseous canal narrowing.

measurements.name: Distraction and displacement
measurements.method: Record translation, interspinous/facet separation or disc-space opening at the named motion segment, with direction, plane and relevant measurements.
measurements.pitfall: Positioning may reduce visible distraction, especially in an ankylosed spine. A vertical laminar fracture alone does not establish posterior tension-band failure.

classification.name: AO Spine thoracolumbar injury classification / TLICS
classification.version: AO Spine thoracolumbar morphology, neurology and modifiers framework (2013); TLICS (2005)
classification.applicability: Traumatic thoracic/lumbar vertebral or motion-segment injury. Classify each injured level or segment separately using the applicable framework.
classification.summary: AO morphology distinguishes compression, tension-band and translational patterns. TLICS uses morphology, posterior ligamentous complex integrity and clinical neurology. Record uncertainty and supplied clinical modifiers; do not fabricate a complete score from imaging alone or turn a label into an automatic treatment recommendation.

pitfalls: A burst fracture requires posterior vertebral-wall involvement; record which endplate or endplates are involved rather than calling every wedge deformity a burst injury.
A vertical laminar fracture accompanying compression does not by itself prove posterior tension-band failure. Assess the entire injury pattern.
MRI oedema without convincing fibre discontinuity can leave posterior ligamentous complex injury indeterminate; signal change alone must not be labelled a definite rupture.
Small anterior separation in an ankylosed spine may conceal a consequential distraction injury. Report the rigid-spine context and acquisition limitations.
Normal-appearing neural structures on imaging do not supply a clinical neurological examination. Unknown neurological status is not an intact examination.

escalation: Promptly communicate traumatic malalignment, suspected consequential tension-band disruption, significant canal compromise or an epidural collection with neural compression through the local trauma/spine pathway.
Report imaging/clinical neurological discordance or an incompletely assessed injury in an ankylosed spine for timely specialist correlation; do not infer clinical neurological status from the images.

steps.label: Level and alignment
steps.detail: Identify each injured level and describe kyphosis, translation or rotation.

normal.NUMBERING, COVERAGE AND ALIGNMENT: Normal thoracolumbar alignment without kyphosis or translation.

findings: Translation of __ mm of [ ] on [ ] (translation or rotation injury).
steps.look: Sagittal CT reformats for alignment and kyphosis; count from a documented reference and correlate ribs and transverse processes.
steps.tip: Translation or rotation in any plane indicates a type C injury, whatever the vertebral body looks like.

steps.label: Fracture morphology
steps.detail: Classify the vertebral body injury as compression, split, incomplete or complete burst, and assess the posterior wall.
findings: Wedge compression fracture of [ ] (AO A1) with __% anterior height loss; posterior wall intact.
Incomplete burst fracture of [ ] (AO A3): one endplate and the posterior wall involved.
Complete burst fracture of [ ] (AO A4): both endplates and the posterior wall involved, with retropulsion.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial CT: anterior column, each endplate and the posterior wall.
steps.tip: Posterior wall involvement separates a burst fracture from a compression fracture; check it on axial and sagittal images.

steps.label: Posterior ligamentous complex
steps.detail: Assess interspinous widening, facet diastasis or dislocation, horizontal posterior element fractures and MRI ligament signal.

normal.POSTERIOR TENSION BAND: Posterior ligamentous complex intact: no interspinous widening, facet malalignment or posterior element fracture.

findings: Interspinous widening and facet diastasis at [ ], compatible with posterior tension-band disruption (AO B2).
Horizontal fracture through the spinous process, laminae and pedicles (Chance-type, AO B1).
Anterior tension-band (hyperextension) injury with anterior disc space widening (AO B3).
MRI: disrupted supraspinous and interspinous ligaments with fluid signal.
steps.look: CT for interspinous distance, facet alignment and posterior element fractures; MRI fluid-sensitive sagittal images for supraspinous and interspinous ligaments and ligamentum flavum.
